Shortcuts

  • Press a layout's shortcut again to move the window on to that layout's next zone. With Split on ⌃⌥1, press it once for the left half and again for the right.
  • Pick the modifier keys every shortcut uses in Settings › Shortcuts: ⌃⌥, ⌃⌥⌘, ⌃⌥⇧ or ⌃⌘. ⌃⌥ stays the default, so nothing changes unless you choose another, and the layouts on your shortcuts stay where you put them.
  • Pressing a shortcut twice in quick succession now moves the window twice, one step after the other. Before, the two moves could run at once and fight, and Restore could then take the window somewhere it had never been.
  • Shortcuts now give a busy app, such as Xcode mid-build, up to a second to answer. Before, a shortcut could leave the window where it was if the app was slow.
  • An app that has stopped responding no longer makes WindowSmith's menu stall when you press a shortcut.
  • With three or more displays, moving a window to the next display now goes to the one that's actually beside it, in the order they sit in Displays settings.

Updates

  • Check for Updates in the menu no longer leaves a WindowSmith icon in the Dock afterwards.
